title: 7. Telecom Disputes Settlement and Appellate Tribunal (TDSAT)

blocks.content: TDSAT was established to adjudicate disputes and protect the interests of service providers and consumers in the telecom sector.

rows: Regulates telecom & broadcasting tariffs and services
Resolves disputes and hears appeals against TRAI orders
Appeals against TRAI lie to TDSAT
Appeals against TDSAT lie to the Supreme Court

items: Appeals against TDSAT orders lie directly to the Supreme Court of India within 90 days, but only on substantial questions of law.
Individual consumer complaints that are maintainable before a Consumer Disputes Redressal Forum do not fall under TDSAT's jurisdiction.
Cyber appellate powers were transferred to TDSAT under the Finance Act, 2017.

blocks.title: Key Takeaways
items: TDSAT was set up in 2000 by an amendment to the Telecom Regulatory Authority of India (TRAI) Act, 1997, to separate regulatory functions from adjudicatory functions.
The tribunal adjudicates disputes between a licensor and a licensee, between two or more service providers, and between a service provider and a group of consumers.
The Chairperson of TDSAT must be a sitting or former Judge of the Supreme Court or a Chief Justice of a High Court.
Under the Finance Act 2017, the jurisdiction of the Cyber Appellate Tribunal and the Airport Economic Regulatory Authority Appellate Tribunal (AERAAT) was merged into TDSAT.
TDSAT is not bound by the Code of Civil Procedure, 1908, but is guided by the principles of natural justice.
